state.final_answer:
**Problem summary**

A 52-year-old man with one year of chronic watery diarrhoea, distal numbness, breathlessness and tiredness has investigations consistent with cardiac amyloidosis, most likely ATTR, but without tissue confirmation or genetic subtyping.

**Interpretation of findings**

The echocardiographic pattern of symmetric left-ventricular wall thickening (septum 14.1 mm), reduced LVEF (36%), grade-II diastolic dysfunction and relative apical sparing on strain is highly suggestive of an infiltrative cardiomyopathy, specifically amyloidosis. The historical NT-proBNP (887 pg/mL) and hs-troponin T (23.9 ng/L) support myocardial stress and injury. Negative serum/urine immunofixation and free-light-chain testing argue against AL amyloidosis. Tc-PYP grade-1 uptake with a heart-to-contralateral-lung ratio exceeding 1.42 is supportive of ATTR but does not meet the higher specificity threshold of grade 2–3 uptake in the absence of a monoclonal protein.

**What remains unestablished**

No tissue biopsy with Congo red staining or mass spectrometry is available to confirm amyloid deposition or type. TTR gene sequencing has not been reported, so wild-type versus variant transthyretin amyloidosis cannot be distinguished. Full blood count, B12 and folate levels remain unobtained, leaving the aetiology of breathlessness and tiredness partly uncharacterised. Current vital signs are not available at this review point.

**Priority next steps**

Tissue confirmation (e.g., fat pad aspirate or endomyocardial biopsy) and TTR genetic testing are needed before assigning a definitive aetiology and subtype.
